Synopsis:
Volo's dialog after the goblin hunt celebration party. Occurs whether tieflings or raiders win, with a variation for whether we've met Volo or not. This is his fallback in being added to our camp.In the tiefling victory variation, Volo is sitting at his desk and thinking/writing an account of our victory that day. As we approach he should set down his pen and turn to speak with us, only returning to work again once he's dismissed us.In the goblin victory celebration, Volo is standing in a cage much like the one in which he is placed in the goblin camp. In this case, he does not wish to be freed. He isn't writing anything or holding anything, but hands off his notes off-screen if intimidated into doing so.

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_GoblinHuntCelebration_Volo.json: This scene is a fallback camp conversation that appears after the goblin‑hunt celebration (it triggers whether the tieflings or the raiders won) and may occur whether you’ve already met Volo or not. In the tiefling‑victory variant he’s seated at a desk, writing an account of the day and will set down his pen to speak before returning to work; in the goblin‑victory variant he’s oddly content to be standing in a cage like the ones used in the goblin camp, not wanting to be freed and not actively writing (he can be pressured into handing off notes). Off‑screen context: Volo is theatrical, ego‑driven and eager to “claim” your deeds — he insists on giving you an iconic nom de guerre and treats your victory as his next story. If the Foundry/“Saved” clusters applied, he is also rattled and grateful from a recent near‑execution and prefers private conversation about sensitive matters.
- GOB_VoloBallad_Volo_Massacre.json: Volo, a reknowned scholar, has been captured by goblins and is being forced to sing on a stage at their celebratory party following a raid. One goblin has the responsibility of guarding him and engages him in conversation. If the goblins are killed, he investigates the corpses, researching the cause of death.
- GOB_VoloBallad_Volo_FestivitiesArea.json: Volo, a reknowned scholar, has been captured by goblins and is being forced to sing on a stage at their celebratory party following a raid. One goblin has the responsibility of guarding him and engages him in conversation. If the goblins are killed, he investigates the corpses, researching the cause of death.
- CAMP_Volo.json: Volo (Volothamp Geddarm) is at the player’s camp after the party intervened at the Steel Watch Foundry — the player tampered with the foundry’s neural switchboard and prevented an explosion that would have killed him. He’s grateful but rattled, having been publicly accused and nearly executed by an angry crowd and hostile agents, so he asked to speak privately rather than risk more exposure. In camp he gives a dramatic warning: he believes Bhaal has returned, names Orin the Red as a possible Chosen who can become the Slayer, and claims a rare tome—A Study of the Slayer by Irenicus—contains the knowledge needed to stop it. Volo is theatrical and prone to absent-mindedness (he treasures the book but may misplace it), earnest about the threat, and eager to recruit a brave adventurer to act.
- GOB_VoloBallad_AD_PleaForHelp.json: Volo recognizes the player as they approach, when he's trapped by goblins and trying to make his own way through the camp without the player's input.

Volo, a reknowned scholar, has been captured by goblins and is being forced to sing on a stage at their celebratory party following a raid. One goblin has the responsibility of guarding him and engages him in conversation. If the goblins are killed, he investigates the corpses, researching the cause of death.

One goblin has the responsibility of guarding him and engages him in conversation. If the goblins are killed, he investigates the corpses, researching the cause of death.

Volo (Volothamp Geddarm) is at the player’s camp after the party intervened at the Steel Watch Foundry — the player tampered with the foundry’s neural switchboard and prevented an explosion that would have killed him. Volo is theatrical and prone to absent-mindedness (he treasures the book but may misplace it), earnest about the threat, and eager to recruit a brave adventurer to act.
